correctness.rationale: For all primes p and arbitrary h1,h2,h3:F_p→F_p, x=r+pt reduces the unnormalized character sum on (x+ph1,x²+ph2,x³+ph3) to p times a sum over derivative-critical residues. For p≥5 a primitive derivative is a nonzero quadratic and at most two p²th roots cannot cancel; for p=2,3 the zero-derivative exceptional cases have incompatible exponent residues so also cannot cancel. Imprimitive sums vanish iff the reduced cubic is a permutation (cyclotomic minimal polynomial). Rootless-derivative and permutation-cubic counts prove nullity 20,168 and p³[p−1+p(p−1)²/2]+(p−1)(1+p1_{p≡2 mod3}) at p≥5; rank p^6−nullity and limit 1/2. Independent exact residue-census reconfirmed p=2,3,5,7,11, incl. rootless/permutation counts; finite checks corroborate but do not prove the universal theorem.
